intervals.label: Phase I: CRES demonstration (University of Washington)
intervals.locator: Project 8 About page, sections "diving deeper" and "Current Experiment status"; DOE Office of Science highlight, 2015-11
intervals.note: Proof-of-concept/R&D demonstration, not a physics-data-taking run; recorded as `commissioning` rather than `active` to avoid overstating its maturity. Start is the year the collaboration first demonstrated CRES (official About page); the University of Washington location comes from the DOE Office of Science highlight (2015). Construction predates 2014 and is not sourced.
intervals.quote: Cyclotron Radiation Emission Spectroscopy (CRES), which was first demonstrated by the collaboration in 2014 ... Phase I in our science program was to demonstrate the feasibility of CRES on single electrons emitted from a gaseous source, Krypton-83m.

intervals.label: Phase II: first CRES measurement of molecular tritium
intervals.locator: Project 8 Phase II apparatus paper (arXiv:2503.08807), abstract
intervals.note: Exact start date of Phase II itself is not stated in the abstract fetched; `start` (2025-03) is the publication month of the paper describing the Phase II apparatus and its first CRES measurement of molecular tritium — an upper bound on when Phase II was already under way, not the phase's true start date. Recorded this way, rather than `start: null`, because a null start with a null end would derive to 'no presence at all' for a phase that is demonstrably active.
intervals.quote: we describe the Project 8 Phase II apparatus, used for the detection of the CRES signal from the conversion electrons of 83mKr and the first CRES measurement of the beta-decay spectrum of molecular tritium

intervals.label: Phase III: atomic tritium R&D
intervals.locator: Project 8 About page, section "Current Experiment status"
intervals.note: No fetched source gives a start date for Phase III; recorded as R&D/proposed rather than construction or active, since the official About page says Phase III will demonstrate free-space CRES and atomic-tritium production and that current efforts are on demonstrators of various technologies, not a running Phase III apparatus.
intervals.quote: In Phase III we will demonstrate the ability to make CRES measurements in free space, as well as the ability to produce and trap atomic tritium. ... Currently, efforts are focused on Phase III.

quantity.quote: the best reported resolution is 15 eV

quantity.note: This is the long-term Phase IV design goal using atomic tritium, not a current achieved sensitivity. The ontology's `mass_energy` dimension does not define a meV unit, so value/unit are recorded in eV/c^2 (0.04) while `display` keeps the source's own wording (40 meV).
quantity.quote: The final phase, Phase IV, will use atomic tritium to measure the neutrino mass with a sensitivity of approximately 40 meV.

name: Project 8
notes: Scope note: this record covers Project 8 overall, with particular attention to the University of Washington / CENPA phase (Phase I CRES demonstration, and CENPA's continuing lead role in atomic-tritium R&D for later phases), per the domain lead's brief.

facility:university-of-washington-cenpa is owned by the 'axions' Wave 3 lead (also used there for ADMX); it now exists (created by that lead during this session) and is referenced here, not duplicated.

Status is recorded PHASE BY PHASE rather than as a single blob, per the brief's caution that early demonstrators must not be called 'active' in the mature-experiment sense: Phase I is `commissioning` (R&D demonstration), Phase II is `active` (physics-relevant CRES measurements on molecular tritium under way), Phase III is `proposed` (atomic-tritium source still in R&D). The record's top-level `status` reflects the most advanced confirmed phase (Phase II, active).

physics_goals.quote: our aim is to measure the absolute neutrino mass using tritium beta decays ... a new method of electron spectroscopy, Cyclotron Radiation Emission Spectroscopy (CRES)
physics_goals.value: Measure the absolute neutrino mass via a high-precision, frequency-based tritium beta-decay spectrum measurement (Cyclotron Radiation Emission Spectroscopy)

summary.plain: An experiment that measures the faint radio signal a single electron gives off when it spins in a magnetic field, aiming to weigh the neutrino. It began as a tabletop demonstration at the University of Washington and is now moving toward using real tritium gas.
summary.technical: Project 8: phased neutrino-mass programme using Cyclotron Radiation Emission Spectroscopy (CRES) on tritium beta decay. Phase I (University of Washington, CRES first demonstrated in 2014) demonstrated single-electron CRES detection on 83mKr conversion electrons (15 eV resolution). Phase II achieved the first CRES measurement of the molecular-tritium beta spectrum. Phase III (CENPA-led atomic-tritium source R&D) targets the systematic limitations of molecular tritium, working toward a final design sensitivity of ~40 meV.

unique_capabilities.locator: Project 8 Phase II apparatus paper, abstract
unique_capabilities.quote: Cyclotron Radiation Emission Spectroscopy (CRES) is a novel technique for the precise measurement of relativistic electron energy.
unique_capabilities.value: Frequency-based (not energy-based) single-electron spectroscopy, measuring the cyclotron radiation of individual beta-decay electrons in a magnetic field rather than their energy directly
